name: United Kingdom
summary: Misuse of Drugs Act 1971 (Classes A/B/C): possessing controlled drugs is a crime. Psychoactive Substances Act 2016 bans supplying other highs (possession legal outside prisons). Drug checking needs a Home Office licence.
callingForHelp: No Good Samaritan law. Ambulance crews don't routinely call police; many forces attend overdoses only if there is a death, violence or risk to crews. NHS confidentiality applies.
drugChecking: Legal only under Home Office licence: The Loop (Bristol, London, events) and WEDINOS (Wales, anonymous postal testing).

lsd.note: Class A: up to 7 years in prison for possession, life for supply.

mushrooms.note: Class A since 2005, fresh or dried. Spores contain no psilocybin and are not controlled.

dmt.note: Class A. Ayahuasca and other DMT-containing preparations are treated as Class A.

mescaline.note: Mescaline is Class A. Owning ornamental cacti (San Pedro, peyote) isn't itself an offence, but preparing them for use is.

dox.note: Class A: DOB, DOM, DOC etc. are covered by the phenethylamine generic definition.

2c-x.note: Class A (2C-B, 2C-I, 2C-E etc. fall under the phenethylamine generic definition).

2c-t-x.note: Class A: 2C-T-2, 2C-T-7 and similar are covered by the phenethylamine generic definition.

5-meo-xxt.note: Class A: 5-MeO-DMT and most 5-MeO tryptamines (incl. 5-MeO-MiPT) fall under the tryptamine generic and ether clauses.

cannabis.note: Class B: up to 5 years for possession; small amounts often get a warning or caution. Medical cannabis only via specialist prescription (since 2018).

ketamine.note: Class B: possession without prescription up to 5 years. ACMD advised (Jan 2026) against Class A; government still considering it (Aug 2026).

mxe.note: Class B (since 2013): up to 5 years for possession.

dxm.note: Not a controlled drug; sold as an over-the-counter cough medicine. Licensed medicines are exempt from the Psychoactive Substances Act.

nitrous.note: Class C since 8 Nov 2023: possessing it to inhale for a high is an offence (up to 2 years). Lawful uses (catering, medical) remain.

amphetamines.note: Amphetamine Class B, methamphetamine Class A. Prescribed ADHD medicines (lisdexamfetamine, dexamfetamine, methylphenidate) are legal with a prescription.

mdma.note: Class A: up to 7 years for possession, life for supply.

cocaine.note: Class A (powder and crack). In Scotland police may give a recorded warning for possession.

caffeine.note: Legal. England plans to ban sales of high-caffeine energy drinks (>150 mg/L) to under-16s from April 2027.

alcohol.note: Legal to buy from 18. Minimum unit pricing applies in Scotland and Wales.

ghb/gbl.note: GHB, GBL and 1,4-BD have been Class B since 13 April 2022 (up to 5 years for possession). Sodium oxybate is a prescription medicine.

opioids.note: Heroin, morphine, oxycodone and fentanyl are Class A; codeine is Class B (low-dose codeine sold in pharmacies). Legal only with a prescription.

tramadol.note: Class C, Schedule 3 since June 2014: possession without a prescription is an offence (up to 2 years).

benzodiazepines.note: Class C: possession without a prescription is an offence. Street 'benzos' such as etizolam are also Class C.

maois.note: Medical MAOIs are prescription-only but not controlled. Syrian rue/harmala aren't controlled, but supply for a high breaches the PSA. Ayahuasca is Class A.

ssris.note: Prescription-only but not controlled: possessing them without a prescription isn't an offence, but supplying them is.
